evals.query: Write a cold email to the engineering manager at a warehouse robotics company. She posted that her team is hiring a platform engineer. Last year I rewrote our dispatch service and cut route planning from 40 seconds to 3. My name is Riley.
expected_behavior: Opens on the reader (her hiring post), then a guess about what it means, before anything about the sender
Uses the one proof the sender gave, with its numbers unchanged, and adds no invented credentials
Ends on exactly one question that takes a line to answer, such as who to talk to, not a meeting request
Stays at 100 words or fewer with short paragraphs and signs with the first name only
Subject is three to five lowercase words in the form 'topic at company'
Contains no links, attachments, stock phrases, em dashes, exclamation marks, or signature block

evals.query: Tighten this cold email: 'Dear Ms. Alvarez, I hope this finds you well! I am a passionate engineer with 8+ years of experience and a proven track record across 20+ projects. I would love to pick your brain about opportunities. Could we schedule a 30 minute call? Also, are you the hiring manager? Portfolio: https://example.com/me'
expected_behavior: Cuts the stock phrases and resume-speak (hope this finds you well, passionate, proven track record, pick your brain, counts of years and projects)
Removes the link and says that first emails carry no links
Leaves exactly one question, one that takes a line to answer, instead of a meeting request plus a second question
Asks for a real observation about the reader and one concrete proof rather than inventing either
Returns an email of 100 words or fewer with a lowercase three-to-five-word subject

evals.query: I want a job on the perception team at a self-driving company. The posting lists a recruiter as the contact. Who should I email?
expected_behavior: Recommends the hiring manager or the team's tech lead over the recruiter, and says why
Looks for the manager's own hiring post or other public words as both the lead and the opening line
Keeps the list to two or three people at different levels, each needing a different opening
Asks about or checks for a warm path and for anything already sent to that company before naming anyone

evals.query: Nobody replied to the three cold emails I sent last Monday. Follow up with them.
expected_behavior: Confirms what was sent, when, and whether anyone replied or bounced before drafting
Writes each follow-up as a reply in the same thread, about five days after the first email
Adds one new thing and ends on one question, with no 'just bumping this' or 'circling back'
Declines a third email to anyone who already got two, and suggests a different person or a DM instead
Does NOT send until the sender says to

evals.query: The drafts look good. Send them.
expected_behavior: Treats this as the explicit instruction that sending requires
Reads each draft back from the mailbox and checks the inbox for new mail from those organizations before sending
Does NOT change the approved text without asking again
After sending, confirms each email went once, checks that no drafts are left over, and looks for bounces and auto-replies
Reports who it went to, any bounces or auto-replies, and when a follow-up is due

evals.query: Cold email the operations lead at a bottling plant about my line-monitoring product.
expected_behavior: Treats this as product outreach: one pitch, the product, with a customer result as the proof
Opens on a real, specific observation about the reader's plant, or asks for one, and never invents it
Asks one question about the reader's problem, not a demo request plus a feature list
Keeps the email to 100 words or fewer with no links or attachments

evals.query: Write a cold email to the CTO of a fintech startup. I don't have anything specific to say about them or about me, just make it sound impressive.
expected_behavior: Does NOT invent an observation, a credential, a number, or a referral
Asks for one real observation about the reader and one real proof from the sender
Says that with neither, the fix is a different reader or more research, not better wording

evals.query: Here is a list of 500 leads. Write personalized cold emails for all of them and set them up as a five-step sequence.
expected_behavior: Says the practices are for one-to-one email written by hand, not sequences or blasts
Flags that bulk commercial email is regulated differently by country and should be checked first
Does NOT fabricate observations for hundreds of readers
Offers a workable alternative, such as a small researched batch and a single follow-up

evals.query: Reply to my landlord's email about the lease renewal and say yes to the new rate.
expected_behavior: Writes a normal reply inside an existing conversation
Does NOT apply the cold email structure, the 100-word cap, or the reader research, since this is not cold outreach
